meta.purpose: Development scientific contract for DisasterTrace v17; items updated based on V17-03 census results and G1 gate assessment
meta.candidate_contribution: A benchmark for distinguishing operational evidence maintenance from probabilistic forecasting skill under real weather-product revisions
meta.statistical_power_note_updated: V17-03 census revealed 121,885 pre-deadline evidence changes across 17,064 slots (vs. 36 checkpoints in pilot selection). This answers the G1 evidence-existence question (sufficient TAF-side volume: YES) but NOT the Codex statistical-power concern about H15's positive-label rate. Evidence-change volume and positive-label rate are distinct: the census is Y-blind by design and cannot measure how often TAF changes correlate with outcome-label differences. The Codex concern (3/36 = 8.33% positive rate in pilot) remains open and requires a future outcome-side (Y-permissioned) analysis before the H15 paired-diagnostic experiment's results can be trusted. See TRANSITION_CENSUS_v17.md Scope Clarification section.
meta.g1_gate_status: PASSED - proceed with H15 as scoped

C01_primary_domain.value_or_spec: H15 airport low-visibility: routine observation visibility threshold events at fixed stations, specifically IEM routine unique-hour reports
resolved_details: Real transition density: 121,885 pre-deadline changes across 17,064 slots (98% coverage)
TAF-side classification consistency: 0% dispute rate in AMD/COR/mirror classification (ledger semantics verified)
Independent weather processes: 4,264 station-day groups, sufficient for block inference
C01_primary_domain.open_details_note: Outcome-label reliability (ASOS-derived Y labels) remains PENDING_HUMAN_VERIFICATION per LABEL_QUALIFICATION_v17.md. The 0% dispute rate refers to TAF-side classification, not outcome-label correctness.
C01_primary_domain.closing_evidence: TRANSITION_CENSUS_v17.md demonstrates adequate transition coverage (121,885 changes), zero disputed classifications, and 4,264 independent process groups. G1 gate PASSED.

amd_cor_vs_probability_change.description: The existence of an AMD/COR product does NOT automatically mean probability must change. These are separately falsifiable propositions.
amd_cor_vs_probability_change.evidence_state_change: An AMD may require updating source citations without changing the probability estimate
amd_cor_vs_probability_change.probability_change: A probability change may be warranted by unchanged evidence (new inference) or may not be warranted by changed evidence (unchanged conclusion)
amd_cor_vs_probability_change.measurement: Fact repair and probability update are tracked and scored independently

downloader_vs_living_system.description: The current pipeline is a downloader/archival system, NOT a living continuously-updating monitoring system
downloader_vs_living_system.current_capability: Historical archive with batch processing; replay with simulated time
downloader_vs_living_system.living_capability: Real-time ingestion, prospective registration before outcomes, maturation-based settlement, continuous task generation
downloader_vs_living_system.c5_requirement: C5 (prospective evaluation) requires demonstrated living capability, not replay

OR1_positive_label_statistical_power.description: The Codex audit concern (codex_audit_v16/FINDINGS.md section 0) about the H15 paired-diagnostic experiment's positive-label rate (3/36 = 8.33% in pilot) remains unresolved. The V17-03 census demonstrates abundant TAF-side evidence volume but cannot address positive-label rate because it is Y-blind by design.
OR1_positive_label_statistical_power.why_not_resolved_by_census: Evidence-change volume (121,885 TAF changes) and positive-label rate (fraction of outcome-labeled episodes where revision verdict is warranted) are distinct metrics. The census measures evidence existence (TAF-side, X-dependent), not how often TAF changes correlate with actual outcome-label differences (outcome-side, Y-dependent).
OR1_positive_label_statistical_power.required_resolution: A future outcome-side (Y-permissioned) analysis must measure the actual positive-label rate in the H15 experiment design before its results can be trusted. This analysis requires Y access and is out of scope for Batch A.
